name: Guatemala
summary: Sky blue, white and sky blue vertical bands with the coat of arms: a resplendent quetzal perched on a scroll bearing the date of independence, over crossed rifles and swords, in a laurel wreath.
origin: Guatemala used the Central American blue and white after independence, then a red-and-yellow conservative flag in the mid-19th century. The liberal government of Miguel García Granados adopted the vertical blue-white-blue flag on 17 August 1871.
The coat of arms was redrawn in 1968 and its details standardised in 1997.

colors.name: Sky blue
colors.meaning: The Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea; also justice and loyalty.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: Peace and purity; the land between the oceans.

symbols.name: Resplendent quetzal
symbols.description: A green bird with a long tail perched on the scroll.
symbols.meaning: Liberty; the quetzal is said to die in captivity. It is also the name of the currency.

symbols.name: Scroll
symbols.description: A parchment reading 'LIBERTAD 15 DE SEPTIEMBRE DE 1821'.

symbols.name: Rifles and swords
symbols.description: Two crossed Remington rifles and two crossed swords.
symbols.meaning: Willingness to defend the country by force; the swords stand for justice and sovereignty.

facts: It is the only Central American flag with vertical bands.
The quetzal is Guatemala's national bird and gives its name to the currency.
The civil flag omits the coat of arms.
clues: Sky blue and white vertical bands with a long-tailed green bird on a scroll.
Its scroll gives a date in September 1821.
Its bird is also the name of the country's currency.
